knowledge:
- key_parameters: y=A cell-by-feature matrix of gene expression values (or an ExpressionSet/SingleCellExperiment object) ;; iter=The number of MCMC iterations to run (default is 2000) ;; burn=The number of MCMC iterations to discard as burn-in (default is iter/2) ;; thin=The thinning interval for MCMC sampling (default is 1) ;; covar=An optional matrix of covariates to adjust for confounding factors
- alternatives: Monocle or Slingshot, which should be preferred if the underlying trajectory has more than one bifurcation or complex multi-branching topologies.
- when_to_use: When analyzing single-cell RNA-seq or qPCR data where cells are expected to transition from a single progenitor state into one of two distinct lineage outcomes (a single bifurcation).
- pitfalls: High-dimensional input matrices (thousands of genes) can lead to extremely slow MCMC convergence; users should pre-filter data to include only transition-associated or highly variable genes (typically 100-500 genes).

workflows.name: mfa_bifurcation_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform Bayesian trajectory inference to estimate pseudotime and branch assignments for single-cell expression data.
input: expression_matrix.csv (numeric matrix of normalized single-cell gene expression values with cells as rows and genes as columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Estimate hyperparameters using empirical Bayes with empirical_bayes ;; 2. Fit the Bayesian mixture of factor analysers model using mfa ;; 3. Extract posterior summary statistics using summary ;; 4. Convert the fit to a tidy format or diagnostic object using to_ggmcmc ;; 5. Plot the inferred bifurcation trajectory using plot_mfa
workflows.code:
# Assuming y is a cell-by-gene expression matrix
m <- mfa(y, iter = 2000, burn = 1000, thin = 1)
ms <- summary(m)
g <- to_ggmcmc(m)
plot_mfa(m)
